LESSON: TIME, DISTANCE AND SPEED

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade seven
Subject: MATHEMATICS
Strand: MEASUREMENTS
Topic 3.5: Time, Distance and Speed
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 8

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Time, Distance and Speed, part of MEASUREMENTS in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade seven MATHEMATICS.

Key inquiry question: Why do we relate distance, time and speed? 2. How is speed important in daily activities?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. identify units of measuring time in real life situations,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Time, Distance and Speed in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. convert units of time from one form to another in learning situations,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Time, Distance and Speed in the Kenya CBC curriculum.

   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Time, Distance and Speed together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Critical thinking and problem solving: A learner develops interpretation and inference skills as they create conversion

tables, relate and determine distance, time and speed.

41

● Self-efficacy: A learner develops personality skills as they observe punctuality in attending to different activities.

Values:
● Patriotism: A learner enhances loyalty as they observe road safety rules, including speed limits.

● Integrity: A learner enhances discipline as they observe punctuality and work out correct distances.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

● Disaster risk reduction (DRR) and safety: A learner observes safety in road and machines in relation to speed.

Link to other subjects:

● Integrated Science: A learner observes time as they carry out different experiments.

● Creative Arts and Sports: A learner participates in athletics during sporting activities.

Suggested Learning Resources:

● Analogue and adapted digital clock, Mater Rule, Tape Measure, Watches, Appropriate Print and Braille Course
